# 🧞 SubtitleGenie {{VERSION}} — the first one!

Welcome to the very first release of **SubtitleGenie**. Drop a movie file on it
and it finds the right subtitles, in whatever languages you want, and either
names them neatly beside your movie or embeds them right into it — 2D or 3D,
one language or all of them, asking you as much or as little as you like.

### 📝 What's in this release

{{CHANGELOG}}

---

### ⬇️ Download & run — no Python needed

Pick the archive for your operating system from the **Assets** below, unpack it,
and run the `subtitlegenie` program inside.

| OS | Archive | How to run |
|----|---------|-----------|
| 🪟 Windows | `SubtitleGenie-{{VERSION}}-windows-*.zip` | Unzip, run `subtitlegenie.exe`, or drag a movie onto it |
| 🍎 macOS | `SubtitleGenie-{{VERSION}}-macos-*.tar.gz` | Unpack, then `./subtitlegenie` in Terminal |
| 🐧 Linux | `SubtitleGenie-{{VERSION}}-linux-*.tar.gz` | Unpack, then `./subtitlegenie` |

### 🚀 Getting started

1. Run `subtitlegenie setup` once. It'll ask for a **free** OpenSubtitles API
   key (from <https://www.opensubtitles.com/en/consumers>) and let you set your
   default languages, whether to save-alongside or embed, and how often you want
   to be asked anything.
2. Then just point it at a movie (or a whole folder):
   `subtitlegenie "My Movie (2014) 3D.mkv"`.

> To **embed** subtitles into movie files you'll also need
> [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) installed. Saving subtitles as
> separate sidecar files works with no extra tools.

### 🐛 Found a problem?

This is a first release — please open an issue with the movie filename and what
happened, and it'll get sorted.
